retweet.text: What I like about the Cybercab is that it only has two seats. In the eight years I lived in Los Angeles and had a Tesla S, I used four seats twice, and two seats four times. So, most of the time I was driving alone. A smaller car that’s safe and drives itself would’ve been fabulous.

quoted.text:
I still can’t believe the entire outer body of the Cybercab is PLASTIC.

I think this is the first production Tesla vehicle built this way.

Tesla molds the COLOR directly into the panels using reaction injection molding.

Far from a traditional paint shop.

A process that can take hours with normal automotive paint can now take minutes.

Tesla says this cuts manufacturing emissions for those parts by around 35% and eliminates the paint VOCs from the traditional process.

And before anyone says, “But what about safety?”

The plastic exterior is not the crash structure.

The massive front and rear giga castings underneath are doing that job.

I rode in the Cybercab myself.

Trust me, it does NOT feel cheap at all.

It actually makes you realize what Tesla is trying to do here.

Fewer parts.

Fewer manufacturing steps.

No traditional paint shop.

Faster production.

Lower cost.

The unboxed process…

This is so much more than Tesla just using plastic to make a cheap car.

Tesla is completely rethinking how you build millions of robotaxis.

I have spent 23 years documenting the global LED transition of city lighting from space.

Across my 4 missions to the ISS, I have photographed every major city on Earth, building a data set of the gradual replacement of sodium vapor lighting with LEDs.

The warmer, yellow-orange of gas discharge lamps has been phased out worldwide to multi-colored LEDs, citing energy savings and environmental reasons.

Widespread adoption has markedly changed the way our cities look from orbit, and as many have pointed out, how they feel to those on the ground!

Here is a collection of the most striking before-and-after photos I have observed:

quoted.text: Miami, Florida as seen from the ISS in 2025. This city has changed tremendously since my previous mission, replacing its yellow-orange sodium vapor lights with multi-colored LEDs. The city grid really pops! This LED takeover of city lighting is world wide. https://t.co/CbbaUH8LV2
